subject: Exec review: Greystone uptime & latency carve-out request
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greystone.io>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@greystone.io>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Greystone - request for uptime & latency commitments

Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the throughput and the control plane features. Before we move our procurement review forward we need explicit commitments around availability and latency for our customer-facing endpoints. High-level asks: 

- 99.99% uptime or an equivalent operational carve-out for the EU/US primary regions
- p95 latency <= 50ms for our inference route (priority model) during business hours (M-F 8am-8pm PT)
- Clear escalation path and on-call contact + runbook for incident classification

Attached is a short matrix with the specific endpoints and traffic profiles. Please let us know whether Redwood can formally commit to these in a contract, or whether we should accept region-level guarantees / fallback behaviors. Procurement wants an answer by Oct 20 so we can include it in our final RFP response.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Best,
Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform Partnerships
Greystone Technologies
Attachment: greystone_requested_uptime_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greystone.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Greystone - request for uptime & latency commitments

Ethan — thanks for the clear asks and the matrix. Forwarding to our infra and legal leads to scope this properly. Quick responses up front: 

- 99.99% global uptime is a high bar for hosted API without dedicated capacity. For hosted we commonly offer 99.95% with clear capacity reservation options under Dedicated.
- p95 50ms is achievable in a dedicated capacity configuration within a single region, assuming model quantization/instance sizing matches Greystone's profile. Global p95 at 50ms is unlikely without regional pinning.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Marcus — can you confirm feasibility and a cost delta for 99.99%/p95-50ms for the priority route if Greystone agrees to dedicated capacity and a 12-month commit?
2) Laura — legal will need to prepare a targeted carve-out and a short redline for our standard SLA (GSY-specific).
3) Ethan — can you highlight which routes must be included in the 50ms commit and whether a staged rollout (prod subset first) is acceptable?

I attached a short internal draft (proposed-carveout-commitment.pdf) that frames options A/B/C so procurement has something concrete to review.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Attachment: proposed-carveout-commitment.pdf (PDF)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greystone.io>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Greystone - request for uptime & latency commitments

Kim / Ethan — dug into the matrix and did a feasibility pass with infra. Summary: 

- Dedicated capacity: we can target 99.99% for the dedicated pool that hosts Greystone's priority model(s), but it requires isolated node groups across two AZs per region and an SLA addendum.
- Latency: 50ms p95 is realistic inside a single region (us-west-2) on A100-equivalent instances with KV cache warmed and continuous batching tuned to Greystone's traffic pattern. Global p95 of 50ms would require multi-region active-active with cross-region routing — cost multiplies significantly and increases N+1 complexity.
- Runbook & on-call: we can provide a named escalation list, 15-min P1 response SLAs, and a runbook for detection -> mitigation.

Cost delta (very high level): 
- Dedicated pool + 2-AZ redundancy: +30-40% ARR on top of hosted run-rate depending on peak token volume.
- Multi-region active-active for global 50ms p95: +2x+ on infra costs.

Proposed compromise: 
- Option A (preferred): Dedicated pool, regional pin (us-west-2), 99.99% uptime for dedicated pool, p95 <= 50ms for priority route, staged to other regions later.
- Option B: Hosted with 99.95% uptime + performance SLAs for peak windows and pref routing; fallback model variant for heavy tails.

I'll attach a technical runbook and a rough cost delta spreadsheet. Ethan — if you can confirm region preference and whether you can accept a staged rollout, we'll lock numbers for Kimberly and finance.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Attachment: technical-runbook-greystone.pdf (PDF)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Greystone - request for uptime & latency commitments

Kim / Marcus — reviewed the proposed wording. Legal notes: 

- We can draft a GSY-specific addendum but need to limit the indemnity exposure and include force majeure carve-outs for third-party infra/network events.
- Recommend a phased SLA attachment: Phase 1 (us-west-2) measurable targets, Phase 2 (other regions) subject to a performance review after 90 days.
- We should include an SLA identifier code (internal reference) for tracking: GSY-EXC-01.

I've attached a redline of our standard SLA with the suggested carve-outs and the clause language for response times and service credits. Please review and flag anything you can't accept from a technical/cost perspective.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Attachment: redline_greystone_sla.docx (Word doc)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@greystone.io>, Procurement <procurement@greystone.io>
Date: 2026-10-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec: Approval required for Greystone uptime carve-out (decision needed by COB 10/20)

Team — Greystone is asking us to sign the addendum with Option A (dedicated pool, us-west-2, 99.99% uptime, p95 <= 50ms for priority route) and is requesting a 30% discount on list pricing in exchange for a 12-month commit. Procurement needs final language and an approval decision by COB today so they can include the commitment in their contracting timeline. 

Summary for execs: 
- Technical: Marcus confirms feasibility in us-west-2 with dedicated pool; multi-region global SLA is out of scope for now.
- Legal: Laura proposes a phased attachment and limited indemnity (see redline).
- Commercial ask: 30% discount + standard onboarding credits. Estimated margin impact: ~20-28% on year-1 depending on token volumes (finance to confirm).

Decision requested: 
1) Approve the carve-out addendum (GSY-EXC-01) for Option A (regional dedicated pool)
2) Approve commercial concession up to 30% conditional on a 12-month commit and prepayment schedule
3) Authorize Laura to finalize SLA redlines and Rishi to approve final commercial terms and send to DocuSign.

I am attaching the compiled packet (proposed-carveout-commitment.pdf + redline). If we don't have sign-off today Greystone may push to a competitor who can offer a different operational model.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Attachments: proposed-carveout-commitment.pdf, redline_greystone_sla.docx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Exec: Approval required for Greystone uptime carve-out (decision needed by COB 10/20)

Kim — thanks for the summary. I approve conditional sign-off on Option A with the following caveats: 

- Finance to confirm the modeled margin impact and provide a final ARR uplift estimate by EOD tomorrow. Do not send DocuSign until finance confirms.
- Legal to sign off on the limited indemnity language; if Legal needs to escalate a specific clause, ping me immediately.
- Marcus: include a final cost + ops runbook as an appendix in the contract (single page) so Greystone has the operational commitments in writing.

If finance confirms the numbers, Rishi approves the 30% commercial concession for a 12-month commit with prepayment. Go ahead and prepare the DocuSign envelope but hold send until we have the finance number.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Note: All attachments referenced above are available in the thread package stored in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/greystone/slas/
